subject: Aurelius POC — request for early-exit carveout & temporary ramp-down safeguard
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@aureliushealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, procure@aureliushealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pilot carveout & ramp repricing (Aurelius POC)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the profiling features. We want to move forward with a 3-month POC but need two contract concessions on the commercial side before procurement can sign: 

1) Early-termination carveout for pilot: Aurelius needs a pilot opt-out with 30 days' notice that converts the account to pay-as-you-go pricing (no lingering committed charges).
2) Temporary ramp-down repricing during pilot wrap: if we reduce committed capacity during/after the pilot, we need a staged ramp schedule with capped downside (no more than 40% step-down in month 1, then 25% month 2, etc.) and a modest transition credit to offset migration effort.

I attached a redline with our proposed language (Aurelius_Contract_Redline_v2.docx) and a short mutual action plan. We are on a tight procurement timeline and would appreciate a commercial + legal read by Friday if possible.

Are you able to route this for an expedited approval?

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Director, Procurement
Aurelius Health
Attachments: Aurelius_Contract_Redline_v2.docx, Aurelius_MutualActionPlan.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: pilot carveout & ramp repricing (Aurelius POC)

Folks — forwarding Aurelius' ask. Summary: 3-month POC, asks for a 30-day pilot opt-out that converts to PAYG and a staged ramp-down schedule with a transition credit. Deal: ~$450k ARR if converted; current ask is pilot-first.

Options I see (trade-offs noted):
- Option A (Conservative): Allow pilot opt-out but require a 60-day notice and a 2-month minimum at 50% committed rate. No credit. Preserves economics.
- Option B (Commercial concession): Approve 30-day opt-out to PAYG, staged ramp-down (40% -> 25% -> 0 over 3 months), and a one-time transition credit (~$20k). Requires exec sign-off as this is outside standard playbook.
- Option C (Conditional pilot carveout): Pilot opt-out allowed only for POC customers < $500k ARR with a required conversion window (if they expand within 12 months they owe remainder of committed spend). Legal will need to add cure/cap clauses and preserve data + audit obligations.

Requesting: Aditya — legal redline / minimum guardrails. Lauren — commercial recommendation and numbers (credit amount, exit fee if any). Markus — executive ok to proceed with Option B (or a modified number).

Deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 | Deal ID: DEAL-2027-0291

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: pilot carveout & ramp repricing (Aurelius POC)

Neha / team — reviewed Aurelius' redline. High-level legal position and proposed clause language below. Key concerns: open-ended opt-outs that eliminate committed economics, unclear data/evidence obligations, and indemnities if they leave mid-rollout.

My suggested guardrails (legal):
- Pilot Opt-Out: Allow a pilot opt-out that converts to PAYG only if customer provides 30 days' written notice and returns any pre-paid credits. Include an explicit "cure period" for material breaches (30 days) before termination for cause.
- Ramp-Down Schedule: Define a maximum step-down of 40% in month 1, then 25% in month 2, then final reconciliation month. If customer reduces more aggressively, apply an exit adjustment equal to 30% of the value of the difference in committed capacity.
- Transition Credit: Cap any one-time credit at 5% of the anticipated first-year committed value for the POC (proposed ceiling ~$25k for this deal).
- Data / Audit: Preserve audit log retention and require a data export window; do not allow deletion clauses that would hinder compliance.

Proposed contractual snippet (can drop into redline):
"During the Pilot Term, Customer may elect to convert to pay-as-you-go pricing upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, subject to the Ramp-Down Schedule and Exit Adjustment set forth below. In the event of early conversion, Customer shall: (i) reimburse any unused pre-paid credits; (ii) be subject to the Exit Adjustment to the extent Customer reduces committed capacity beyond the Ramp-Down Schedule; and (iii) cooperate with data export and audit procedures as reasonably requested by Redwood.

Ramp-Down Schedule: Month 1: up to 40% reduction; Month 2: up to 25% reduction; Month 3: final reconciliation. Exit Adjustment: 30% of the value of capacity reductions that exceed the Schedule.
"

I can incorporate this into a redline. If commercial wants more concession on credit, we need explicit exec approval and a clear timebox to the POC only.

—Aditya
General Counsel (Acting), Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: pilot carveout & ramp repricing (Aurelius POC)

Neha / Aditya / Markus — commercial read here. Background: Aurelius is a mid-market healthcare buyer with a credible expansion path; this POC is strategic for our reference set in health. They are price-sensitive but likely to convert if POC goes well.

Recommendation (balanced): Approve Option B but with tighter financial guardrails:
- One-time transition credit: $15,000 (applied against first invoice if they convert within 6 months).
- Ramp-Down: allow 40% / 25% / reconciliation schedule per Aditya's language.
- Pilot opt-out: allow 30 days' written notice but require a 2-month deminimis minimum usage charge equal to 50% of the committed rate in month 1 to cover provisioning.
- Exit fee: if customer fully terminates before 90 days after conversion, apply 20% of remaining committed value as an administrative exit fee.

If Markus signs off I will notify Aurelius and provide the commercial terms to be captured in the MSA redline. Given the reference potential I think $15k credit + these guardrails is reasonable.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: pilot carveout & ramp repricing (Aurelius POC)

Team — thanks for the clear options. I approve proceeding on the basis of Lauren's Recommendation with the following modifications and conditions: 

1) Reduce transition credit to $12,500 (final).
2) Keep the Ramp-Down schedule and the 30-day pilot opt-out, but drop the 2-month 50% minimum; instead require a 60-day notice or payment-in-lieu equal to 30% of month 1 committed value.
3) Retain the 20% administrative exit fee if they terminate within 90 days of conversion.
4) Legal to finalize redline with Aditya's Exit Adjustment language and data retention clauses.
5) This concession is approved as a one-time exception tied to Deal ID DEAL-2027-0291 and expires if the MSA is not executed within 21 days.

Neha — you have my conditional sign-off to communicate the revised commercial terms to Aurelius; make it explicit this is an exceptional concession and subject to final legal wording. Please loop me in on the counter-signed MSA.

-Markus
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
